title: EV Trends: The Shift Goes Mainstream
subtitle: Sales, markets, costs and what comes next

slides.title: EV Trends: The Shift Goes Mainstream
slides.subtitle: Sales, markets, costs and what comes next
slides.speaker_notes: This deck covers the state of the global electric vehicle market: how fast it is growing, where the growth is coming from, why costs are falling, and what that means for us.

slides.title: Global EV sales grew roughly eightfold in five years
bullets: About 1 in 5 new cars sold worldwide in 2024 was electric
Growth continued even as several markets cut purchase subsidies
Plug-in hybrids gained share alongside battery-electric models

chart.title: Global electric car sales (BEV + PHEV)
chart.source_note: Source: IEA Global EV Outlook 2025 (approximate figures)

slides.speaker_notes: The curve has not flattened. Even in a year where some subsidies were withdrawn, sales still grew by roughly a quarter. Electric cars are now a mainstream product, not a niche.

slides.title: China accounts for nearly two-thirds of EV sales

chart.title: Share of global electric car sales, 2024
chart.source_note: Source: IEA Global EV Outlook 2025 (approximate shares)

slides.speaker_notes: China is both the largest market and the largest producer. Europe is second, while the US remains a smaller share. Emerging markets are small but growing fastest from a low base.

slides.title: Battery pack prices have fallen about 85% since 2013
bullets: Batteries are the single largest cost in an EV
Cheaper LFP chemistries and scale drove the 2024 drop
Price parity with petrol cars is near in many segments

chart.title: Average lithium-ion battery pack price
chart.source_note: Source: BloombergNEF battery price survey (approximate, real terms)

slides.speaker_notes: Falling battery costs are the engine behind everything else. Once pack prices settle around 100 dollars per kWh, electric cars can match petrol cars on upfront price without subsidies.

slides.title: Key takeaways
bullets: EVs are mainstream: about 20% of global new car sales
China leads on both demand and manufacturing scale
Battery cost declines are closing the price gap with petrol
Charging access and grid readiness are the next bottlenecks
slides.speaker_notes: The question for us is no longer whether the transition happens but how fast, and where we position ourselves in it. Happy to take questions.
